claim: The occupation is the root; Israel doesn't want peace.

heard.who: António Guterres, UN Secretary-General, to the Security Council, 24 October 2023
heard.quote: The Palestinian people have been subjected to 56 years of suffocating occupation.

heard.who: Marwan Barghouti, Palestinian leader, in The Guardian, 2015
heard.quote: The real problem is that Israel has chosen occupation over peace, and used negotiations as a smokescreen to advance its colonial project.

answer: In August and September 2005 Israel removed all 21 of its settlements from inside Gaza, about 8,000 settlers, and withdrew its soldiers. In January 2006 Hamas won the Palestinian parliamentary election. In June 2007, after fighting with Fatah, Hamas took complete control of Gaza. Israel then closed the crossings and imposed a blockade, and Egypt closed its border too. Israel says the blockade is about stopping weapons. The UN and the Red Cross say Gaza is still occupied because Israel controls its borders, airspace and sea; Israel says it is not occupied since it has no forces inside. So the 2005 withdrawal was real, and so was what followed it. Both facts belong in the story.

contested: Is Gaza still occupied? The ICRC, the UN, the International Court of Justice (in its July 2024 advisory opinion) and many academics say yes: Israel kept control of Gaza's land crossings, airspace and territorial waters, so occupation law still applies in proportion to that control. Israel says no: after 2005 it had no forces or settlers inside and the Strip is not occupied; some legal experts, including many from military backgrounds, agree that occupation needs troops on the ground. Both positions are on this card.

Why the blockade. Israel says it is needed to stop Hamas importing weapons and to protect its civilians from rocket fire; the Anti-Defamation League and Israeli officials say goods were misused for military purposes. UN agencies and human rights groups say it harms civilians and is collective punishment. Egypt also closed its crossing.

Whether the 2005 withdrawal was a peace step. Israel called it unilateral and not negotiated. Critics say it was done for Israel's own reasons, not as part of a deal; Elie Podeh's 2025 study argues it was coordinated with the Palestinian Authority and others but that Israel did not use it to advance peace talks and the Authority did not curb armed groups.

Hamas won an election the US and Israel had accepted taking place; the Quartet then demanded recognition of Israel, an end to violence and acceptance of past agreements, and Hamas refused, after which aid was frozen. How much that contributed to the 2007 clashes is disputed.
not_claimed: It does not claim Israel's withdrawal ended the conflict or that Gaza was not under Israeli control afterwards in any sense.
It does not claim the blockade is lawful or unlawful; courts and experts differ.
It does not cover the wars after 2008 or 7 October 2023.
It does not claim Hamas's takeover was caused only by Israel, or only by Palestinians.
